message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** and **Cloud Resource Manager API** must be enabled.  
> * You need a GPU quota for the region you choose (e.g., `us-central1`).  
> * The `gcloud` CLI must be installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * If you use the REST API, you’ll need an OAuth 2.0 access token (`gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`).

---

## 1.  `gcloud` CLI – one‑liner

```bash
gcloud compute instances create my-gpu-instance \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Compute zone (pick one that has GPU quota). |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-a6000` is the RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB. |
| `--metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true` | Auto‑installs the NVIDIA driver on first boot. |

> **Tip** – If you want a pre‑emptible instance (cheaper but can be terminated), add `--preemptible`.

---

## 2.  REST API (cURL)

### 2.1  Build the JSON payload

Save the following to `instance.json` (replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` and `YOUR_ZONE`):

```json
{
  "name": "my-gpu-instance",
  "machineType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true" }
    ]
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

### 2.2  POST the request

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/instances"
```

> **Note** – The access token expires after ~1 hour. For long‑running scripts, refresh it or use a service account key.

---

## 3.  Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU is attached:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh my-gpu-instance --zone=us-central1-a --command="nvidia-smi"
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Quota exceeded** | Request a GPU quota increase in the Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Quotas. |
| **Driver not installed** | Ensure `install-nvidia-driver=true` metadata is set. |
| **Wrong GPU type** | Use `nvidia-a6000` (not `nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| **Region mismatch** | GPU availability varies by zone; pick a zone that supports A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`). |

That’s it! You now have a fully‑functional Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy GPU computing!
